card.summary: We don't have a file size limit, but larger files will take time to process and can have a higher chance of failing if your internet connection is interrupted.

free_tier.stated: We don't have a file size limit, but larger files will take time to process and can have a higher chance of failing if your internet connection is interrupted.

per_object_cap.stated: No file size limit; the duration of a video file cannot be longer than 12 hours.
per_object_cap.notes: The video-publishing page says there is no file size limit but caps file duration at 12 hours.

retention.stated: Account deletion permanently deletes all data tied to the account from Spotify's server; a show not distributed to other platforms is deleted immediately, and removal from other platforms can take up to 10 business days.
retention.notes: The account-deletion article states permanent deletion of account data, immediate deletion of a show not distributed elsewhere, and up to 10 business days for removal from other platforms.

egress.terms: Free and unmetered via Spotify's own CDN (d3ctxlq1ktw2nl.cloudfront.net). No egress meter, no per-download charge, no plan upgrade that changes it.

record.tooling: No documented public upload API. Content uploads are restricted to web and mobile dashboard interfaces. Read access is available via public podcast RSS feeds (`https://anchor.fm/s/<showid>/podcast/rss`) without authentication.
record.chaining: Unlimited shows per Spotify account (the UI has 'Add a new show' with no published cap) x unlimited episodes x no file-size limit. Also accepts video (MP4/MOV/MPG) on the same free tier, so the payload need not be audio at all.
record.limits_note: Format allowlist is narrow: audio must be MP3, M4A or WAV, mono or stereo; video MOV/MPG/MP4. Uploads are single-shot HTTP from the browser, so a dropped connection mid-upload fails the episode ('higher chance of failing if your internet connection is interrupted'). There is no resumable/chunked API, which is the real ceiling on file size in practice.
record.reliability_note: RE-ENCODES everything to 128 kbps stereo. Verified live: enclosure for an episode with itunes:duration 00:52:22 declared length=50272965; the staging object at d3ctxlq1ktw2nl.cloudfront.net/staging/2026-9-21/434650861-44100-2-6d67ddd17af0f.mp3 returns 206, Content-Range 0-1023/50272965, and its first 1 KB is a bare MPEG frame with no ID3 header at all. 50,272,965 x 8 / 3142 s = 128,003 bps. Exactly 128 kbps CBR. The '-44100-2-' in the filename is the ingest normaliser's fingerprint (44.1 kHz, 2 channels). Your WAV or 320k MP3 does not survive. Second caveat: anchor.fm enclosures are 402/302 chains through anchor.fm/s/<id>/podcast/play/<n>/<urlencoded origin>, so the enclosure URL is a redirector with the object path embedded. Permanent, but the served object is always the transcode.
